text:
maya: quick heads-up: pushed a prototype of a new synthetic generator that mixes fractal long-tail interarrivals + concentrated microbursts. aiming to repro the kernel-selection p99 regressions we saw on nightly. PR: https://git.internal/rw/inference/pulls/7621 :eyes:
lina: link? can you paste the exact command you used to run the harness? want to reproduce locally.
maya: sure - toy command i used:
```
./bin/traffic-gen --pattern=fractal-surge --qps=250 --burst-multiplier=6 --tail-alpha=1.4 --seed=8675309 --duration=10m 
```
also ran with `--kv-warmup=60s` and `--batch-delay-ms=3` to mimic production TTLs.
ajay: nice. two quick things to watch: 1) kernel switch overhead when batch sizes oscillate, 2) KV cache hit ramp shape. did you capture kernel switch counters?
maya: yes, added tracing for kernel_switch_count and switch_time_us. baseline run (no patch) kernel_switch_count ~ 1.2k over 10m, avg switch_time_us 48us. with the new batching heuristic it jumped to ~2.9k and switch_time_us median 62us. p99 latency changed from 320ms -> 343ms in that run.
zhen: that suggests we're thrashing small-batch vs large-batch kernels. what are your batch size distributions?
maya: here's an excerpt from the generated histogram (batches per minute): 
- size 1: 7.6%
- size 2-4: 42.1%
- size 5-16: 34.7%
- size 17+: 15.6%
I tuned the surge multiplier which increases small single-request spikes during burst peaks.
lina: for apples-to-apples we should pin kernel selection to the baseline decision path and re-run to isolate batching heuristic impact. run both: `--kernel-policy=baseline` and `--kernel-policy=adaptive` and compare. also set `--fixed-seed` so stochastic effects are controlled.
ajay: +1. also measure KV cache effective hit ratio over time. if KV hit is < 50% during the first minute you'll see a p99 tail from KV cold misses. record `kv_hit_ratio` as a time-series at 5s cadence.
maya: captured kv_time_series, initial warmup 0.12 -> steady 0.72 after ~90s. p99 spikes correlate with windows where kv_hit_ratio < 0.4. attaching quick grep output: 
```
[00:00:10] kv_hit_ratio=0.12 p50=22ms p99=420ms
[00:01:30] kv_hit_ratio=0.56 p50=20ms p99=190ms
```
this suggests replay harness warmup is too short for our workload.
zhen: can we change generator to perform prefix priming of KV during ramp phase? something like synthetic ‘prefill’ that requests 1000 distinct keys spread across shards before main ramp.
lina: yeah, implement `--kv-prefill=<n>` that hits the same key distribution as the replay. for apples-to-apples compare runs prefill=0 vs 1000 vs 5000.
ajay: one more: instrument per-token kernel latency when model length > 256 vs <= 256. some kernels we pick are better for short sequences and degrade for long. that interacts with batching because longer sequences keep workers busy longer and delay switches.
maya: added `per_token_kernel_profile.csv` to the run artifacts. notable: attention_kern_a p50=12us p99=180us for seq<=256, but for seq>512 p99=420us and kernel selection moved to fallback path.
perf-bot: CI run for PR 7621 finished: baseline vs pr7621 (10m fractal-surge): p50 delta -0.6%, p95 delta +1.7%, p99 delta +7.1% (regression). artifacts: https://ci.internal/rw/artifacts/7621/
lina: ugh 7.1% p99 is significant. do we know whether most of that is from KV cold windows or kernel switch thrash?
maya: on the failing runs I profiled flamegraphs. top contributors: kernel_switch overhead (~21%), tail serialization in the runtime (~18%), plus a few percent from scheduler queue wakeups. KV cold windows accounted for ~27% of the highest single p99 spikes (but not the sustained shift).
zhen: sounds like a hybrid issue: the batching heuristic causes more frequent kernel decisions which increases switch overhead; meanwhile some windows have KV cold misses compounding the p99. proposed mitigations: 1) reduce sensitivity of adaptive heuristic (increase hysteresis), 2) add compact prefill before ramp, 3) add a lightweight cache-hint header to keep hot KV keys alive in workers for additional 60s.
ajay: agree with ordering: 1st try hysteresis tuning + baseline kernel pin to measure impact. then simulate prefill. we should run a small matrix: kernel_policy {baseline, adaptive}, hysteresis {low, medium, high}, kv_prefill {0,1000}. 6 runs x 10m each.
lina: i'll schedule the matrix on the staging cluster tomorrow morning. also suggest measuring CPU steal/SMT interference on nodes, sometimes kernel switch cost balloons under hyperthread contention. set `NODE_AFFINITY=exclusive` for one run to compare.
maya: thanks. i'll update the PR with a smaller default `--batch-delay-ms` behavior and add `--kv-prefill` flag. also adding clearer metrics to the harness: kernel_switch_count, kernel_switch_time_us_p50/p99, kv_hit_ratio_ts, batch_size_histogram.
deploy-bot: deployment to perf-stage queued for 2026-03-19T09:00Z (job id 8857).
ajay: when we have the staged results, let's annotate them inline on the PR and decide if we revert the heuristic or tune it. plan for rollback if p99 > 5% regression on apples-to-apples.
lina: copy. tagging @zhen for kernel-affinity follow-up. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all — will post run links once the matrix completes and attach flamegraphs for the worst-case runs.
